machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.3 (bundled, static); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: 7.25.5 and 7.25.20 each built whole from their own tree (a git worktree of the tag for 7.25.5; the same .config, compiler and external libraries): the benchmarks of performance/c/ and the ctest binaries test_topic_pkey_integer, test_topic_pkey_integer_iterator2 and test_topic_pkey_integer_iterator5. The two binaries of each benchmark run alternately, the order flipped every round, with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run: 8 rounds, 24 for the three ctest binaries. Mean +- standard deviation (median). Unlike the 7.25.5 report, no module was padded or relinked: a whole-release build also moves where the code lands, so a change under ~2.5% on an append is not told apart from placement.
method.tag_run: The absolute figures are the 7.25.20 side of the same run, on the build of 7.25.20: 8 rounds (24 for the ctest binaries), no CPU pinning. The per-second benchmarks drop their first and last second; reads page by page are the FORWARD pass.

story.title: Yuneta 7.25.20: the treedb a quarter faster, and nothing slower
story.lead: 7.25.20 closes the fifteen releases since the last report (7.25.5): fixes to the agent, the file watcher, the TCP writes, the `SWITCHS` macro and the masking of secrets. None of them was meant to change speed, and one of them is the largest gain of the round: `SWITCHS` stopped compiling a regular expression every time a switch was entered, so treedb writes run 16-25% faster and 40 treedbs start twice as fast. Measured against 7.25.5 on the same machine, each release built from its own tree, the two run alternately. No figure got slower beyond the spread of its rounds.

hero.text: faster: starting 40 treedbs whose schema did not change takes 0.32 s, down from 0.67 s with 7.25.5. Every yuno with treedbs pays it at each start, and the gain came from the fix of a memory leak, not from tuning.

treedb: link or unlink two nodes
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built twice, from the tree of each release, and the two binaries run alternately: 8 rounds, 24 for the three timeranger2 tests. A change inside its whisker is noise. Everything is on one axis: the change of the time an operation takes.
story.prices_sub: What got slower, how much, and what it buys.
story.no_prices: None this time. No figure of 7.25.20 is slower than 7.25.5 beyond the spread of its rounds. The closest, 600 000 appends to one key (+3.6%, at the edge of the spread), runs append code that did not change between the two releases; the main append benchmark, 24 rounds, moved +0.3%.
